lot: 1.B.1 (Phase 1, P0) — pure addition of events/listener/service/migration; NO call-site wiring (deferred to 1.B.2 which needs a frozen-zone gate).
finding_origin: F-01 (audit) + NEW-05 (second-opinion GPT-5.4-pro): when an order is canceled or refunded, the daily_consumed_qty on ItemBranchAvailability is NEVER released. Repeated cancel/refund cycles accumulate phantom consumption that wrongly 86s items. Must support: (a) full cancel, (b) partial refund (line-item level, with quantity), (c) idempotency under duplicate event delivery (3 identical OrderCanceled events must release exactly once).

Iterates $order->orderItems, decrements daily_consumed_qty on ItemBranchAvailability, sets is_available=false + unavailable_reason='out_of_stock' when daily_consumed_qty >= max_daily_qty. Dispatches ItemAvailabilityChanged::forBranch only on the flip (was available → now 86).

scope_files_to_modify: app/Services/Menu/AvailabilityService.php (ADD method releaseForOrderItems(array $lineItems) — DO NOT touch decrementForOrder)

OrderCanceled.constructor_args: public readonly Model $order (Model = FrontendOrder OR Order; the order must have ->id, ->branch_id, ->orderItems relation accessible).
OrderCanceled.no_payload_array_needed: The full order is passed; the listener loads orderItems and releases all line items.
OrderCanceled.broadcasting: NOT broadcast — internal domain event only.

RefundCreated.constructor_args: public readonly Model $order, public readonly array $refundedItems where each entry is ['order_item_id' => int, 'qty' => int]. If $refundedItems is empty, listener treats it as 'full refund' and releases ALL line items (same behavior as OrderCanceled).
RefundCreated.broadcasting: NOT broadcast — internal domain event only.

release_method_contract.lineItem_shape: ['order_item_id' => int, 'item_id' => int, 'branch_id' => int, 'qty' => int] — caller (listener) builds these from $order->orderItems + the requested release qty.
release_method_contract.idempotency_strategy: For each line item: SELECT order_items.id, quantity, released_qty FOR UPDATE; compute deltaQty = min(requestedQty, quantity - released_qty); if deltaQty <= 0 → log info 'release skipped (already released)' and continue; else: ItemBranchAvailability row → daily_consumed_qty = max(0, daily_consumed_qty - deltaQty); if was unavailable AND now daily_consumed_qty < max_daily_qty → flip is_available=true, unavailable_reason=null, dispatch ItemAvailabilityChanged::forBranch(itemId, branchId, true, 'released_after_cancel_or_refund'); update order_items.released_qty += deltaQty, released_at = now().
release_method_contract.transactions: Wrap the full operation in DB::transaction.
release_method_contract.after_commit: ItemAvailabilityChanged dispatch must occur AFTER the transaction commits. Use DB::afterCommit(fn() => event(...)) inside releaseForOrderItems, OR collect events and dispatch them at the end of the listener after the transaction commits — your choice, document it in implementation_steps.

listener_contract.ReleaseAvailabilityOnOrderCanceled: Receives OrderCanceled. Loads $order->orderItems. Builds the full lineItems array (qty = each line's full quantity). Calls AvailabilityService::releaseForOrderItems.
listener_contract.ReleaseAvailabilityOnRefundCreated: Receives RefundCreated. If $refundedItems is empty → load full $order->orderItems and behave like full cancel. Else: filter $order->orderItems by the order_item_id keys and use the qty provided. Call releaseForOrderItems.

tests_required: StockReleaseFullCancelTest — Setup an item with max_daily_qty=10, decrement by 5 (consumed=5, available=true), then dispatch OrderCanceled → assert ItemBranchAvailability.daily_consumed_qty=0 (rebound to 0 because 5-5=0), assert order_items.released_qty=5 each line.

StockReleaseFullCancelTest 86-flip — Item with max_daily_qty=5, decrement by 5 (consumed=5, available=false). Dispatch OrderCanceled → assert daily_consumed_qty=0, is_available=true, ItemAvailabilityChanged event dispatched (use Event::fake([ItemAvailabilityChanged::class])).

StockReleasePartialRefundTest — Order with 1 line of qty=5. Dispatch RefundCreated with refundedItems=[['order_item_id'=>X,'qty'=>2]] → assert order_items.released_qty=2 (NOT 5), daily_consumed_qty=consumed-2.

StockReleaseIdempotencyTest — Dispatch OrderCanceled twice on the same order → assert release happened exactly once: order_items.released_qty equals the original quantity (NOT 2x); daily_consumed_qty correctly decremented once; ItemAvailabilityChanged dispatched at most once on the flip (use Event::fake assertions on count).
StockReleaseIdempotencyTest — Dispatch OrderCanceled then RefundCreated (full) → second one is a no-op (released_qty already maxed).
non_negotiable_constraints: branch_id isolation — releaseForOrderItems queries MUST filter by both item_id AND branch_id (never cross branches).
After-commit dispatch — ItemAvailabilityChanged from releaseForOrderItems MUST fire AFTER the DB::transaction commits.
OrderStatus enum — never write magic int statuses; reuse App\Enums\OrderStatus.
Pricing SSOT — N/A (no pricing logic touched).
Frozen zones — DO NOT touch FrontendOrderService, PaymentService, OrderService.
Listener idempotency — must be safe to retry / re-deliver. The released_qty column is the truth ledger; never trust the event alone.
acceptance_criteria_measurable: Full cancel of an order whose item was 86'd → item flips back to available, daily_consumed_qty correctly reduced, ItemAvailabilityChanged dispatched once via after-commit, order_items.released_qty matches each line's quantity.
Partial refund of 2 units out of 5 → daily_consumed_qty -= 2; order_items.released_qty = 2; remaining 3 units still consumed.
Duplicate OrderCanceled (or duplicate RefundCreated) → released_qty does NOT exceed quantity; daily_consumed_qty does NOT go below 0; ItemAvailabilityChanged dispatched at most once on the flip.
Mixed sequence (OrderCanceled then RefundCreated full) → second listener invocation is a no-op (logs 'release skipped').
All 4 tests above pass via `php artisan test --filter=StockRelease`.
No existing test regresses (run `php artisan test --filter=Availability` and `php artisan test --filter=Kiosk`).
